Okay. Hate me for this if you like. It's actually stupidly simple.

Rotate the page clockwise about 30 degrees. Hold the pen between your thumb and middle finger, with you index finger resting on top, so you form a loose claw. With the page so tilted, you can place your hand directly beneath your text, and still see what you're writing, and where you're going. Use your fingers to form the letters, but move your forearm to shift your hand across the page. Your wrist should stay relaxed and mostly straight. The heel of your hand should glide along the page, not be the primary support, which is something I did for a long time, and I'm sure you are familiar with it.

It will take practice, sure. But it comes remarkably quickly. And if you want to try something really wacky, open a notebook, and start writing right to left. You'll be amazed at how easily it comes.

This technique is better suited for the Palmer method - cursive writing. It's kind of cumbersome for block printing. Also, start with a felt-tipped pen. It will help you detect when you're pressing too hard, and you won't suffer because of the insane angle you'll be holding the pen at.
